title: Fenn and the Sky Puddles
markdown:
The Fernflake Mountains are a place where sunlight dappled through leaves like spilled honey and the air smelled of sweet damp moss. Here lived Fenn, a young ogre whose skin was the gentle colour of a spring fern, still unfurling towards the sun. His eyes were as round and curious as pebbles tumbled smooth in a stream. Fenn was not like the ogres in the grumbly old tales; he loved quiet mornings, the soft sigh of the breeze, and the gentle patter of tiny paws exploring the world.

His most treasured companions were Pip, a fluffy white kitten with sparkly blue eyes, and Willow, a little round puff of brown fur with a tail that wagged like a happy question mark when she was pleased. Fenn loved nothing more than to take them for slow happy walks in the bell-fern woods, where the giant ferns unfurled their fronds like sleepy green snails stretching in the sun.

One sun-drenched morning Fenn hummed a low rumbly tune. Pip’s bright blue eyes spotted a butterfly. Whoosh. Pip, a white blur of pure excitement, darted off after the fluttering marvel. Fenn chuckled, a warm rumbling sound. Pip was always so quick. Fenn trusted Pip to be back soon. Mama said to watch him carefully, a little voice whispered, but it felt far away. Willow trotted along beside Fenn, her fluffy tail a bouncy happy rhythm against the soft moss.

That’s just a sky-trick. The real sky is up there. Fenn would need those words soon.

They wandered a little further than usual, past the whispering pines that always sounded as if they were sharing secrets, and over a carpet of moss so soft and squishy it felt like walking on a hundred tiny pillows. Suddenly Fenn stopped. He felt a stillness settle around him, like a quiet breath held by the forest. Before them lay a puddle, but this was no ordinary puddle. It was a perfect shimmering mirror, so clear it reflected the vast bright blue sky above as if a piece of heaven had fallen right onto the forest floor. It was so real, you could almost feel the warmth of the sunbeams on your face.

“Oh, look.” Fenn’s voice was a soft rumble. He felt a little wobble in his tummy, a familiar feeling he knew as concern. Mama always said to be careful. He gently scooped up Pip, who was staring, mesmerized, at the sky-puddle. “Not today, Pip. That’s just a sky-trick. The real sky is up there.” He pointed a big gentle finger upwards, towards the endless blue. Pip blinked his bright blue eyes, a tiny bit confused, but he snuggled into Fenn’s warm chest.

Fenn set Pip down a safe distance away, and they continued their walk. The bell-fern wood hummed with the busy buzz of bumblebees and the cheerful chirping of unseen birds. Then, from deeper in the woods, they heard a sound, a merry bubbling sound, like laughter bubbling in a pot.

“Ho ho. More shimmer-berries. Delicious, delicious.”

Peeking through the tall feathery ferns, Fenn saw a small round goblin, no bigger than a prize pumpkin, stirring a big bubbling pot. He had a bright red nose that wiggled with joy with every stir. This was Grooble, the renowned jam-maker of the Fernflake Mountains. His little hut, tucked away amongst the roots of an ancient oak, was covered in colourful jars, all smelling wonderfully sweet and fruity.

“Hello there.” Grooble’s voice was as warm and rich as his famous jam. “Fancy a taste of my famous shimmer-berry jam? It is the finest in the mountains, made with sunshine and whispers of the forest. Guaranteed to bring a smile.”

Fenn smiled, a wide gentle smile. “Hello, Grooble. That smells absolutely delightful.” He knew Grooble was a kind goblin; all the forest folk knew Grooble and his generous spirit.

Pip, however, was utterly captivated by the sweet fruity aroma. His little kitten nose wiggled and wiggled. He followed the yummy smell with his eyes. As Grooble turned to add a fresh handful of plump shimmer-berries to the pot, Pip, quick as a wink and light as a feather, darted towards a small waiting jam pot sitting on a mossy stump nearby. And what did that jam pot hold, precariously close to Pip’s eager paws? Another perfect sky-blue puddle, looking just like the one they had seen earlier.

“Pip, no.” Fenn’s voice was still gentle but with a touch more urgency. Pip darted towards the sparkly puddle. Fenn’s big hand reached out, but then he paused. It looked so much like the sky. Maybe just a quick peek would not hurt? A silly thought, but it made his tummy do a little flip. To keep Pip safe, Fenn willingly pushed aside his own moment of quiet, reaching for the little kitten. He would taste the jam himself later. With a quick smooth movement, faster than a hummingbird’s wing, Fenn carefully guided Pip away from the edge of the jam pot, away from the tempting sky-puddle. Pip stumbled a little, surprised by Fenn’s sudden firm but loving touch. Fenn held him close for a moment. “That looks like sky, little one, but it is just the water showing what is above. The jam is in here.” He tapped the pot gently. “And it is very yummy and real.”

That’s just a sky-trick. The real sky is up there.

Grooble chuckled, a deep rumbling sound that made his red nose wiggle. “Ah, a curious kitten. Always looking for adventure, aren’t you, little cloud-ball? I like your spirit.” He scooped a tiny bit of glistening jam onto his finger. “Here, my friend. Have a proper taste. Not from the sky, but from my pot.” He offered the jam to Pip, who eagerly lapped up the sweet sparkly goodness. Pip purred like a tiny happy motorboat. Fenn watched, a happy sigh escaping him. He carefully gave Willow a little dab of jam on a broad leaf, which she licked with great satisfaction, her tail giving a contented thump-thump on the moss. Then Fenn himself tried some. Oh, it was scrumptious. It tasted of wild berries bursting with flavour and the warm golden glow of the sun.

“Thank you, Grooble. You make the most wonderful jam. It is truly the taste of sunshine.”

“And you,” Grooble winked, his good eye twinkling like a fallen star, “take good care of your little explorers. They have such brave hearts for such tiny creatures.”

As the sun began to dip lower, painting the Fernflake Mountains in breathtaking hues of rose and gold, Fenn, Pip, and Willow made their way home. Fenn held Pip securely in his arms. Pip looked at a shiny leaf on the path. Fenn gently pointed. “That is a shiny leaf, Pip. Not a toy.”

And as the moon began to peek shyly through the branches, Fenn kept walking. The jam taste stayed on his tongue. The sky stayed up where it belonged.
characters: Fenn (young ogre who walks the bell-fern woods), Pip (a fluffy white kitten with sparkly blue eyes)
